items.title: Sid Davilla Interview, 1969-04-17
items.q: Is that guy probably French? Must have been, yeah. ... I don't know. I'd have to look up some pictures.

ctx.x: Yeah, contrary to a lot of, to many people's opinion, we call it two beat, two four Dixieland music. It's associated with that. And the thing that surprised me the most is that these guys, for the most part, lay down a heavy four beat rhythm, you see. Just a punching style, you know, just a pounding style. And one of the few, a few musicians that I work with, I got to know very well, that had a light two beat style was Ray Badouk, Monk Hazel, you see. But for the most part, take Paul Barberin, you know, he laid…
The guy that calls himself now probably French, I can't remember. He's the leader of the band, which has called itself the Celestan Band. I'm not sure whether he was playing for them then, maybe.

I don't know. I'd have to look up some pictures. We managed to keep some pictures, which I should have taken more of, because, believe me, they're treasured. And, uh, Celestan would be up there playing with these high, high-button shoes, and, uh, the band would be just driving. It sounded like a herd of elephants going down the street with a banjo and the piano playing four. Four, now, no two-beat on the piano rhythm, but just a straight-four drive, you know? And it had a tremendous, exciting effect. And it was a…
